content:
Apple is set to launch several new Macs later this year, including the first-ever touchscreen MacBook and the first models powered by the M6 chip. Here's everything we know so far about the upcoming new Macs.

MacBook Ultra

The flagship Mac launching later this year will be the first Mac in Apple's history to feature a touchscreen. Whether this new machine will be called the MacBook Pro or MacBook Ultra remains unknown, but it will be the biggest MacBook Pro redesign in years.

According to reports, Apple is testing a high-end MacBook model on macOS 27.1, with an expected release at the end of October.

This brand-new MacBook will be Apple's first model to feature a touchscreen and OLED display. It is also expected to drop the notch design in favour of a Dynamic Island-style design similar to the iPhone. Bloomberg has also reported that the new high-end MacBook will be thinner than the current MacBook Pro.

In terms of performance, the new touchscreen MacBook will use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the current MacBook Pro.

M6 MacBook

According to reports, Apple plans to launch the first Mac with the M6 chip later this year. The company is developing an updated base-model MacBook Pro equipped with the next-generation M6 processor.

According to reports, the M6 will offer faster memory bandwidth, along with improvements in CPU and GPU core performance.

Aside from the M6 chip, the new base-model MacBook Pro is not expected to feature any other changes.

iMac

Apple last updated the 24-inch iMac in October 2024, upgrading the chip from M3 to M4. Apple is currently working on the next iMac update, which is reportedly set to launch this autumn.

The new iMac is expected to feature Apple's upcoming M6 chip. There are also rumours that the new iMac will offer a brand-new range of colour options.

Mac mini and Mac Studio (Possibly)

Lastly, Apple is also developing updated models of the Mac mini and Mac Studio, but the release dates for these machines remain uncertain.

According to reports, Apple is testing a new Mac mini lineup powered by M5 Pro and base M6 chips. Meanwhile, the Mac Studio is being tested with M5 Max and M5 Ultra processors.

According to Bloomberg, the release dates for these models are still unclear and will depend on "memory chip supply conditions." The general expectation had been for the new Mac Studio to launch by year-end, but it now appears that remains subject to change.

The current Mac mini offers M4 and M4 Pro chip options, while the Mac Studio comes in M4 Max and M3 Ultra configurations.

Summary

Affected by memory and storage constraints across the industry, Apple's Mac lineup is currently in a rather awkward position. Nevertheless, the company still has several powerful new models in the pipeline. What are your thoughts on the new Macs launching before year-end? How much do you think the MacBook Ultra will be priced at? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
